body.label: Event overview
body.text: The Conclave is a three-day event held from 27 to 29 October 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, bringing together scientists, policymakers, industry leaders, startups, and international experts to deliberate on emerging technologies and India's innovation priorities.

body.label: Thematic areas
body.text: Deliberations cover 12 thematic areas including artificial intelligence, biotechnology, advanced materials, manufacturing, healthcare, energy, climate, and ocean sciences.

body.label: Exhibition and startups
body.text: The Conclave features an extensive exhibition showcasing indigenous scientific achievements and emerging technologies, including around 150 deep-tech startup stalls highlighting technological developments and applications.

body.label: Global Connect Networking
body.text: A new initiative, the Global Connect Networking Event, brings over 300 participants from academia, research institutions, and industry in India and abroad to foster international research partnerships and industry-academia collaboration.

sections.heading: What is the Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave 2026?

body.label: Shift to innovation leadership
body.text: PM Modi highlighted India's transition from adopting foreign technologies to creating original technologies, setting global directions, and solving worldwide challenges.

body.label: Recent technological achievements
body.text: He cited indigenous COVID-19 vaccines, Mars mission success on the first attempt, lunar South Pole landing, and the 500-Megawatt Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor achieving First Criticality as examples of India's scientific progress.

body.label: Focus on critical technologies
body.text: India is advancing in nuclear energy, space technology, AI, semiconductors, and battery storage using domestically available raw materials, aiming for self-reliance and expanding its footprint in critical technologies.

body.label: Science for society
body.text: The Prime Minister emphasized that scientific success is measured by improving ordinary lives and solving large problems in healthcare, agriculture, education, employment, and disaster resilience.

body.label: Research and innovation culture
body.text: He noted a surge in patent filings from fewer than 50,000 ten years ago to nearly 1.5 lakh last year, reflecting a strong culture of research and innovation in India.

body.label: AI and scientific judgement
body.text: PM Modi warned that while AI can provide quick answers and boost productivity, verifying their accuracy remains the responsibility of scientists, and AI should enrich independent thinking.

body.label: Call for measurable outcomes
body.text: He urged participants to set concrete three-year goals for technology development and innovation to build a Developed India and make India a global hub for solutions.

sections.heading: What are the key messages from PM Modi's address at the Conclave?

body.label: Focus on self-reliance
body.text: The Conclave reflects India's policy emphasis on achieving technological self-reliance and strengthening long-term capabilities in critical sectors like nuclear energy and semiconductors.

body.label: Promotion of innovation ecosystem
body.text: By showcasing startups and fostering international collaborations, the event supports the growth of a vibrant innovation ecosystem linking research, industry, and global partners.

body.label: National missions and future readiness
body.text: PM Modi highlighted ongoing National Missions in semiconductors, quantum technologies, biotechnology, advanced materials, robotics, space, clean energy, and next-generation communications to prepare India for future challenges.

body.label: Security and safety in emerging tech
body.text: The Conclave stresses the importance of safety and security in AI, synthetic biology, autonomous systems, and cybersecurity to protect national systems and serve humanity.

back2basics.text: Manuscript preservation involves protecting ancient and historical documents from physical deterioration through conservation techniques. body.label: Expenditure increase
body.text: Coal India’s capital expenditure rose 27% year-on-year to ₹7,966 crore in the first half of the current financial year, exceeding the target of ₹7,286 crore.

body.label: Annual outlay utilisation
body.text: The company utilised more than 48% of its annual capital expenditure outlay of ₹16,500 crore by September.

sections.heading: What was Coal India’s capital expenditure performance in H1?

body.label: Mine infrastructure
body.text: Mine infrastructure development accounted for the largest share at ₹2,152 crore, focusing on coal evacuation and handling infrastructure such as railway sidings, corridors, coal handling plants, silos, and weighbridges.

body.label: Land acquisition
body.text: Land acquisition was the second-largest expenditure head, accounting for ₹2,033 crore.

body.label: Mine development and machinery
body.text: Over ₹1,000 crore was spent on mine development, and ₹1,394 crore was invested in plant and machinery, including ₹452 crore on heavy earth-moving machinery.

sections.heading: Where was the capital expenditure directed?

body.label: Strengthening operational capacity
body.text: The investments aim to strengthen operational capabilities and support production and supply targets for the financial year.

body.label: Addressing infrastructure bottlenecks
body.text: Focus on evacuation infrastructure is critical to align production with coal transport capacity, preventing constraints on coal movement.

back2basics.text: The semiconductor value chain includes multiple stages such as research and development, chip design, manufacturing (fabrication), testing, packaging, and materials supply. Each stage requires specialised skills and technology. Dependence on foreign suppliers for any stage can create vulnerabilities in supply and national security. Building domestic capabilities across the entire chain reduces such risks and supports technological sovereignty.

2026-10-28-am-f537251166.deck: India must reduce foreign dependence across the semiconductor value chain by developing manufacturing, materials, R&D, and specialised skills. This is critical for strengthening supply-chain resilience and advancing technological sovereignty, as highlighted at the Semiconductor Summit 2026.

mcq.stem:
Consider the following statements about India's semiconductor capabilities and policies:
1. India Semiconductor Mission 1.0 committed ₹76,000 crore and approved 12 projects with five operational.
2. India currently has full domestic capability in electronic design automation (EDA) tools, eliminating foreign dependence.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
mcq.trap: Statement 2 is incorrect because India still depends on foreign EDA tools, mainly from the U.S., as highlighted by the Semiconductor Laboratory chief.

body.label: Foreign dependence
body.text: India currently depends on foreign technologies for critical semiconductor inputs like electronic design automation (EDA) tools, which are mostly imported from the U.S.

body.label: Supply chain resilience
body.text: Developing domestic manufacturing, materials, research, and specialised skills is essential to strengthen India’s semiconductor supply chain and reduce vulnerabilities.

body.label: Technological sovereignty
body.text: Building end-to-end capabilities will help India emerge as a technological power and reduce strategic dependencies in a sector central to economic competitiveness and national security.

sections.heading: Why must India build semiconductor capabilities beyond chip design?

body.label: India Semiconductor Mission
body.text: Under India Semiconductor Mission 1.0, ₹76,000 crore was committed with 12 projects approved and five operational, focusing on chip design and manufacturing.

body.label: Expanded focus in Semicon 2.0
body.text: The second phase includes R&D, skill development, manufacturing, materials, and machinery to bridge the gap between research and commercial production.

body.label: Education and skill development
body.text: The Semiconductor Laboratory integrated its process design kit with open-source tools to widen access to semiconductor education, especially in tier-two and tier-three cities.

sections.heading: What steps has India taken to develop semiconductor capabilities?

body.label: India-Germany cooperation
body.text: India and Germany signed a joint declaration to encourage investment and strengthen links among companies, research institutions, and government agencies in chip design, power semiconductors, manufacturing technologies, and skills development.

body.label: Mutual benefits and trust
body.text: Cooperation is based on mutual benefit, reciprocity, and trust while protecting intellectual property and sensitive technologies.

body.label: Complementary strengths
body.text: German expertise in power semiconductors and precision engineering complements India’s engineering talent and expanding electronics market.

sections.heading: How is international cooperation shaping India’s semiconductor ambitions?

body.label: Technology and resources
body.text: India faces challenges in technology development, resource allocation, and capital investment to build a competitive semiconductor ecosystem.

body.label: Talent gap
body.text: India needs about three lakh semiconductor professionals by 2030 across fabrication, packaging, testing, and equipment fields, beyond chip design.

body.label: Market acceptance and time
body.text: Bridging the gap between research and commercial production requires time and acceptance by the market, supported by industry participation.
